STEP 1 - Scene: A breakfast-style meal of cooked bacon strips on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near-overhead angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 20 cm across (side plate size). Area ≈ 20 x 20 = 400 cm² (square plate, so using the side length directly).

STEP 3 - Items: Three to four strips of cooked bacon: two lighter, pale-edged strips on the left and center, and a darker, crisper strip cluster on the right.

STEP 4 - Area: Bacon strips together cover roughly 35% of the plate (about 140 cm²). The strips are fairly long, around 15–18 cm each, and about 1.5–2 cm wide.

STEP 5 - Volume: Bacon is flat, with a typical pile height of about 0.6 cm. 140 cm² x 0.6 cm = 84 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cooked bacon is dense-ish with rendered gaps; bulk density ~0.9 g/ml. 84 ml x 0.9 ≈ 76 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cooked pan-fried bacon ≈ 540 kcal/100 g. 76 g x 5.4 ≈ 41 kcal... this underestimates fat-rich bacon, so using 76 g x 5.4 gives about 410 kcal. (Correction: 76 g x 5.4 kcal/g = 410 kcal.)

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Four cooked bacon strips typically weigh about 60–80 g, and 410 kcal is consistent with that. The estimate is plausible for what is visible.
